A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Geo-Sign research. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G are readable and matchable despite revisions and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original CSL-Daily translation experiments, ablations, embedding analyses, computational profiling, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds How2Sign translation, WLASL2000 recognition, and Gaussian pose-noise experiments.

M1.justification: The ST-GCN/mT5 architecture, hyperbolic projections, pooling, token attention, losses, and optimization remain unchanged. The expanded attention equations and pseudocode restate operations already documented in v1, including Appendix C.2.2 and the code listings. No recognition-specific algorithmic adaptation is described.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from CSL-Daily translation to American Sign Language translation on How2Sign and isolated recognition on WLASL2000. v2 also reports YTASL pretraining for ASL and introduces corrupted-pose testing on CSL-Daily. These extend language, task, training-data, and input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: The CSL-Daily comparator set is retained. Tables 2–3 introduce reported comparisons against additional methods, including GloFE-VN, YouTube-ASL, SLT-IV, SignMusketeers, SSVP-SLT, ST-GCN, SignBERT, SignBERT+, HMA, BEST, NLA-SLR, and Sign-Rep; these were not evaluated comparators in v1.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include per-instance and per-class Top-1 recognition accuracy and a Gaussian corruption sweep with noise levels from 0.00 to 0.05 before ST-GCN processing. ASL experiments introduce YTASL initialization. Existing CSL-Daily settings remain unchanged, although ASL fine-tuning details and the precise noise-scale definition are underspecified.

E4.justification: Table 4(c) adds a focused robustness analysis comparing Geo-Sign and Uni-Sign under increasing Gaussian pose noise. The existing curvature and loss-weight ablations, embedding analyses, computational profiling, and qualitative error examples are retained.

E5.justification: The seed-42 disclosure is unchanged in v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 7, as are the existing plotting practices. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the new results.

E6.justification: Existing CSL-Daily scores remain unchanged, including Geo-Sign's 27.42 BLEU-4 and 57.95 ROUGE-L. Newly reported results include How2Sign scores of 40.8/15.1/35.4 for BLEU-1/BLEU-4/ROUGE-L, WLASL2000 accuracies of 63.64/61.89 per instance/class, and noise-robustness results. These are additional experimental outcomes, not revised performance under v1's retained settings.

T1.justification: The geometric definitions, Fréchet-mean convergence proposition, distance-gradient derivation, and appendix mathematics are retained. New numbered attention equations in the main text express operations already present in v1's explanation and Appendix C.2.2; they add no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal methodological contributions remain unchanged. The introduction newly claims applicability to ASL and isolated recognition, while the conclusion expands the demonstrated language scope from CSL-Daily to Chinese and American Sign Language.

C2.justification: v2 attributes noise robustness to larger geodesic margins and the strongest RGB How2Sign comparator's advantage to pretraining scale. The relocated limitations omit v1's explicit pose-estimation-dependence sentence. A new inference-cost statement in Section 3.4 conflicts with the retained Appendix F.1.1 statement that the hyperbolic branch is unused at inference.

D1.justification: v2 specifies YTASL-pretrained ST-GCN weights for ASL and where Gaussian corruption is applied. The detailed appendix hyperparameters, hardware, training time, preprocessing, code listings, and code-access statements remain essentially unchanged; a complete ASL-specific reproduction recipe is not added.

R1.justification: References are added for the new comparisons, including GloFE, SignMusketeers, WLASL, HMA, BEST, NLA-SLR, and SSVP-SLT, while Section 2's research positioning remains largely unchanged. The Two-stream network reference disappears although the TS-SLT table entry remains; its v2 citation instead points to C2RL.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the token-attention explanation, separates contrastive loss from alignment methods, and subdivides the experimental discussion. References move before the appendices, and limitations/future work move to Appendix F.3. Most narrative and appendix prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn to show token keys, attention, and contextual aggregation more explicitly. Two benchmark tables are added, and the ablation display expands from two panels to three. Figure 2 is relocated and qualitative tables are repaginated; the underlying diagnostic plots in Figures 2–5 are retained.

improvement.justification: The ASL and pose-noise experiments partially address v1's untested generalizability and pose sensitivity, and the revised attention explanation improves clarity. The net gain is limited by incomplete new protocols, absent uncertainty for small recognition gains, and an unexplained clean Uni-Sign score of 26.25 in Table 4(c), unlike Table 1's test baselines. The new inference-cost statement also introduces an internal contradiction. These weaknesses temper the useful expansion of empirical support.
